clue.text: Worker about to fight — watch out

indicators.note: about means going round, so the worker's letters surround the fight

parts.note: a worker is a bee, the classic worker insect
to fight is to make war

explanation.surface: A labourer is warned off before a scrap breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: Beware is the warning imperative telling someone to be careful, the same as watch out.

clue.text: Monk who founded an order at foot of Scottish mountain

indicators.note: in a down clue, being at the foot means placed below, so the order follows the mountain

parts.note: ben is the Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
an edict is an official order or decree

explanation.surface: A monk established his religious order at the base of a Highland peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an order' looks like part of the definition (the Benedictine order) but supplies EDICT.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Benedict of Nursia founded the Benedictine monastic order in the sixth century.

clue.text: Street name needs changing — it's a bit flowery

indicators.note: the word name must be altered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A road sign's name must be altered because it sounds too fancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs changing' turns NAME into AMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamen is the pollen-bearing part of a flower, literally a bit of a flower.

clue.text: Unusual glee shown after getting a pass in school

indicators.note: the rearranged glee comes after the pass in the answer

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of glee set out in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone shows rare delight on passing an exam at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' turns GLEE into LEGE. 'pass' suggests an exam but is a mountain pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A college is a place of education, a kind of school.

clue.text: Copper band used for healing

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A copper bracelet is worn as a folk remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Curing a patient is making them well, which is healing them.

clue.text: The look and smell of a summer house?

parts.note: a gaze is a long look
BO, body odour, is an unpleasant smell

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a garden pavilion looks and smells like.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small open garden building, a summer house for sitting outdoors.

clue.text: One's tried for military and domestic offence

definitions.text: One's tried for military and domestic offence

parts.words: One's tried for military and domestic offence
parts.note: an offence that can bring a soldier before a court martial and also counts as abandoning one's spouse

explanation.surface: Something gets you court-martialled and in trouble at home too.
explanation.walkthrough: Abandoning one's post is a military crime; abandoning a spouse is a domestic one, grounds for divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: Desertion is both leaving the armed forces without permission and wilfully abandoning a husband or wife.

clue.text: Country artist interned by government out east

indicators.note: being interned means being shut inside, so the artist goes within
out means the letter for east is put out of the word for government

parts.note: rule is government, as in British rule
RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A national painter is locked up by an administration expelled from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like a noun for a nation, but it is the adjective. 'out' drops the east letter from the word for government, and 'interned by' puts the artist inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural means relating to the country as opposed to the town, the adjectival sense of country.

clue.text: Riverside plant?

parts.note: plant read as an industrial works rather than vegetation growing on the bank

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what grows along the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a reed or willow, but it is a factory, one driven by the river's flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill whose machinery is powered by a water wheel stands beside a river, a riverside works.

clue.text: Clergyman inwardly pious? The reverse — a treacherous type

indicators.note: the reverse tells us to read the whole construction backwards
inwardly means the clergyman has the pious word inside him

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a clergyman
pi is a slang abbreviation for pious

explanation.surface: A vicar who appears devout within is actually the opposite, a two-faced rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The reverse' looks like a comment on piety (a hypocrite), but it tells you to read the clergyman-around-pious construction backwards; 'inwardly' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A viper is a figurative name for a treacherous, spiteful person, like a snake in the grass.

clue.text: Stick together in a difficult situation

explanation.surface: People cling together when things get tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Bind means both to tie or fix together and, informally, an awkward predicament.

clue.text: Gracious! Happen to have one over the eight, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is spoken and its sound gives a differently spelt word

parts.words: Happen to have one over the eight
parts.note: to happen is to be, and one over eight is nine, so be nine

explanation.surface: An exclamation as someone turns out to be a little drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is British slang for slightly drunk; here it is literally nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign means kindly and gracious in manner.

clue.text: Leaving child constitutes misconduct

parts.note: going means leaving or departing
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Running away from home counts as bad behaviour for a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Goings-on is an idiom for questionable or improper behaviour.

clue.text: An ugly comparison?

parts.note: what something is said to be as ugly as, in the stock simile

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a comparison to describe ugliness.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'as ugly as sin' supplies the comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: The fixed simile as ugly as sin uses a moral wrong as the standard of ugliness.

clue.text: Born of woman

parts.note: the French word for born, used before a married woman's maiden name

explanation.surface: A biblical-sounding phrase about human birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Born of woman' echoes the Book of Job, but it means 'born', said of a woman's original surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Née, French for born, introduces a married woman's maiden name, so it is used only of women.

clue.text: Sack member after finding smuggled goods

parts.note: to boot someone out is to sack them
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: An employee is dismissed after contraband is discovered.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootleg describes illicitly made or smuggled goods, originally liquor hidden in boot tops.

clue.text: A kiss, which may transport one

definitions.meaning: a kiss, the old word ..., which the setter spells with one S

explanation.surface: A kiss that sweeps someone off their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' suggests rapture after a kiss, but means carry. The kiss sense rests on buss, here given one S.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is a public road vehicle that transports passengers; buss is an old word for a kiss.

clue.text: Expression of approval the Spanish love to come up with

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
love is zero in tennis scoring, so the letter O

explanation.surface: Spaniards love to come out with a word of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come up' turns ELO backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Olé is the Spanish cry of approval heard at bullfights and flamenco.

clue.text: Former graduate set up test paper

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the graduate is placed upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A one-time graduate prepares a test paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns MA into AM.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is an examination, a written test paper.

clue.text: Go ahead with borrowed money

explanation.surface: Proceed with a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Advance means both to proceed forward and a sum of money lent or paid ahead of time.

clue.text: Acceptance of notice before election

indicators.note: before places the notice ahead of the election in the answer

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
an option is a choice, and election can mean choosing

explanation.surface: A motion is approved after a notice is posted ahead of a vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'election' suggests a vote but means a choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption of a proposal is its acceptance or taking up.

clue.text: It is pressed into use when distribution by air is required

definitions.text: It is pressed into use when distribution by air is required

parts.words: It is pressed into use when distribution by air is required
parts.note: a can whose nozzle is literally pressed to spray its contents through the air

explanation.surface: Something is put into service when items must be sent by airmail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressed into use' reads as called into service, but the button is literally pressed; 'distribution by air' suggests airlift, not spraying.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a pressurised spray can, operated by pressing, dispersing fine droplets into the air.

clue.text: Accommodation for poor sailors?

parts.note: sailors read as passengers at sea, poor as short of money, not bad at seamanship

explanation.surface: Someone asks where incompetent seamen are housed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor sailors' suggests the seasick or unskilled, but means low-paying passengers on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest part of a passenger ship, where the poorest travellers were housed.

clue.text: Turn at the wheel yachtsman initially found awkward

parts.note: a trick is a spell of duty at the helm of a ship

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of yachtsman is taken

explanation.surface: A sailor finds a stint steering the boat difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: A trick at the wheel is a sailor's shift steering, a nautical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricky means difficult to handle, which is awkward.

clue.text: The whole country is full of conservationists

indicators.note: being full of means containing, so the country holds the conservationists

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
the NT, National Trust, is a British conservation body

explanation.surface: An entire nation is packed with environmentalists.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means whole, complete, with nothing left out.

clue.text: Conducted research in favour of retirement?

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
retiring for the night means going to bed

explanation.surface: Someone investigated the case for stopping work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests leaving work, but means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe is to investigate closely, so probed means investigated or conducted research.

clue.text: Pleads, we hear, for approval

indicators.note: we hear means the word for pleads is spoken and gives a differently spelt word

parts.note: to pray is to plead or beg earnestly

explanation.surface: A supplicant begs for a favourable verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise is expressed approval or commendation.

clue.text: In the right niche, possibly make one better off

indicators.note: in means the letter for right goes inside the rearranged word
possibly signals niche is only one arrangement of its letters

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Finding the right niche might make someone rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns NICHE into ENICH, and R goes between its N and I.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich someone is to make them wealthier, better off.

clue.text: Pool made by domestic pet

definitions.meaning: a pool is a shared fund of money
a pet name for a cat

explanation.surface: A swimming pool built by the family cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitty means both a communal fund of money and a familiar name for a cat.

clue.text: Retreat on being put in command

indicators.note: being put in means on is inserted inside the word for command

parts.note: mastery is command or control, as in command of a language

explanation.surface: Someone is sent on a retreat after being placed in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' suggests withdrawal, but is a religious refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery is a place of religious seclusion, a retreat from the world.

clue.text: Go round in a woman's garment

definitions.meaning: a garment hanging from the waist

explanation.surface: Someone does a lap dressed in women's clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Skirt means to go around the edge of something and a garment worn from the waist down.

clue.text: Game for a drink after hard work

indicators.note: after places the drink later in the answer than the hard work

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
op, short for opus, is a work
a Scotch is a glass of whisky

explanation.surface: Someone is offered a whisky as reward for tough labour.
explanation.walkthrough: Hopscotch is a children's game of hopping across chalked squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a playground game played by hopping across numbered squares.
